candidates.name: Kaposi sarcoma
support_spans: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch
30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of a purpuric patch and plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches is consistent with Kaposi sarcoma.

candidates.name: angioma
support_spans: Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
candidates.why: The histopathological findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes are suggestive of an angioma.

candidates.name: Kaposi sarcoma
support_spans: Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors
candidates.why: The immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors and the presence of pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei are consistent with the pathophysiology of Kaposi sarcoma.

candidates.name: hemangioma
support_spans: Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
candidates.why: The presence of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes is suggestive of a hemangioma.

candidates.name: Kaposi sarcoma
support_spans: Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
Ki-67 proliferation marker analysis performed
candidates.why: The positive staining for CD31 and negative staining for CK5, along with the Ki-67 proliferation marker analysis, are decisive findings for Kaposi sarcoma.
